title: Introduce perceptual-tone delta tokens and altitude-mapped shadows for responsive density
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Dense data surfaces (tables, dense sidebars, compact action lists) are suffering perceptual contrast regressions when we apply the same neutral token steps across UI scales. Current elevation/shadow tokens are visually inconsistent between small and large components and across light/dark modes. Goal: Ship a token set and migration path that (1) introduces perceptual-tone delta tokens to create predictable tonal steps across sizes and contexts, and (2) replaces the existing 'shadow-depth' tokens with altitude-mapped shadows (shadow.altitude.*) that scale consistently with component density and ambient lighting. Deliverables include token spec, usage guidelines for buttons/tables/charts, CSS/Sass token exports, design-to-code token generator, and codemods for migration.
acceptance_criteria: New perceptual-tone delta tokens defined for light and dark modes with delta values validated in Lab space
Altitude shadow token set (shadow.altitude.0..8) implemented and documented with cross-browser fallbacks
Design library (Figma) updated with tokens and 1:1 mapping to exported CSS variables
Migration codemod and token-lint rule detect deprecated tokens and auto-migrate common cases for buttons, rows, and cards
Visual regression tests (perceptual diff) for key pages show no more than 1% color delta after migration or clearly justified changes
Accessibility checks: contrast ratios for text over new surfaces meet AA for primary content and at least large-text AA for secondary content
migration_steps: Phase 1: Add new tokens as opt-in aliases (e.g., --tone-delta-1, --shadow-altitude-1) and keep legacy tokens active
Phase 2: Release design library updates and publish token docs; ship codemod v0.1 for quick-win patterns (buttons, card surface, row background)
Phase 3: Run token-lint across component repo, open PRs for remaining deprecated tokens, and run visual regression suite
Phase 4: Flip default variables in a controlled canary release and monitor visual regressions and support tickets
Phase 5: Deprecate legacy token names after two cycles and provide automated migration reports
